title: Detecting Anomalies Using Z-Score Approach
description: Identify **anomalous transactions** where the transaction amount is more than **2 standard deviations** above or below the customer's mean transaction amount. Show the transaction, the customer's mean and std, and the z-score.
solution_sql: WITH stats AS (SELECT customer_id, AVG(amount) AS avg_amount, STDDEV(amount) AS std_amount FROM transactions GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT t.transaction_id, t.customer_id, t.amount, ROUND(s.avg_amount, 2) AS customer_mean, ROUND(s.std_amount, 2) AS customer_std, ROUND((t.amount - s.avg_amount) / NULLIF(s.std_amount, 0), 2) AS z_score FROM transactions t JOIN stats s ON t.customer_id = s.customer_id WHERE ABS((t.amount - s.avg_amount) / NULLIF(s.std_amount, 0)) > 2 ORDER BY z_score DESC

test_cases.description: 2 anomalies: C1 transaction of $900 (z≈2.04) and C2 transaction of $1800 (z≈2.04). C3 has no outlier.

hints: Compute per-customer AVG and STDDEV in a CTE, then join back to the transactions table to calculate z-score = (amount - avg) / std for each transaction.
Filter WHERE ABS(z_score) > 2 to find outliers — use NULLIF(std_amount, 0) to avoid division by zero for customers with zero variance.
explanation: The CTE computes per-customer statistical parameters. Z-score = (value - mean) / std_dev measures how many standard deviations a value is from the mean. Customer 1: 5 normal ≈$100 + 1 outlier $900; mean≈233.67, std≈326. Z for $900 ≈ 2.04 > 2. Customer 2: 5 normal ≈$200 + 1 outlier $1800; z ≈ 2.04 > 2. Customer 3: tightly clustered $48–$55, no outlier. Two anomalous transactions detected.
